title: A prompt cannot be sent while a turn is running
body:
`App`'s prompt key handling ignores Enter while `transcript.in_flight` is set and leaves the text in the box. A turn stays in flight until the agent answers `session/prompt`. With the Claude adapter, that includes the time Claude spends waiting for a background agent to finish. During that wait you can type but cannot send.

The Claude adapter v0.101.0 accepts a `session/prompt` while another is running. Its `initialize` response declares `_meta.claudeCode.promptQueueing: true`. In the adapter, `startTurn` pushes the new prompt onto the session's input and onto a turn queue, and answers each `session/prompt` when that prompt's turn ends. A `session/cancel` cancels every prompt received before it.

## Proposal

- When the agent declares `promptQueueing`, Enter during a turn sends the prompt right away. The transcript shows it marked as queued.
- When the agent does not declare it, coax holds the prompt and sends it when the running turn ends.
- `in_flight` stays set until the agent has answered every prompt sent.

## Open

- How does coax learn that Claude has started on a queued prompt, so it can drop the queued mark? This needs a trial against the adapter.
- Should Esc cancel the queued prompts along with the running turn? A `session/cancel` to the Claude adapter cancels them all.
close_reason: Done in f8d9f51. Enter during a turn sends to an agent that declares `claudeCode.promptQueueing` and holds the prompt for one that does not. Waiting prompts show in a queued row, and Esc returns them to the box. Not done: advertising the `backgroundSubagents` AIR capability, which would end turns while subagents run but brings turns the agent starts on its own.
